title: Sharding

validation.research: Six official primary references from Microsoft, MongoDB, Citus and Vitess. Sharding is established horizontal distribution of different row subsets across owning storage groups, potentially replicated internally. Distinguishes same-host partitioning, vertical column separation and full-data replication; preserves former Horizontal Sharding title as alias. Capacity is the central design problem, so Performance and Scalability is the single primary home. Key placement, virtual buckets, targeted/scatter-gather requests, tenant co-location, cardinality/frequency/monotonicity, hot keys, migration and shard-local versus cross-shard guarantees are addressed. Existing useful order/tenant7/bucket6/mapv12/B and telemetry/resharding context retained.

example_limits: Existing canonical data-horizontal-sharding revised in place as Sharding with former title Horizontal Sharding as alias. Preserve ID/route, exact summary, attribution, old tags/Data Engineering membership and primary figure path. One primary home moves from Storage & access to Performance and Scalability; former collection retains cross-link and fourteen other members. Retain order, tenant7/bucket6/mapv12/B, tenant co-location, telemetry hotspots and safe movement context. Original Python sequential in-memory directory uses twelve fixed logical buckets and four groups, with D initially empty. Positive numeric tenant classifier (tenant-1)%12 is deliberately illustrative, not a production hash. Tenant7/orderO71/paid moves from B at version12 to D at13 while calls are paused; the old write is rejected before row mutation and fresh read returns paid, old B copy absent. Global-version authoritative validation is coarse and invalidates unrelated cached routes; physical copies during quiescence do not grant two active writers. Immutable strings and tuple tenant/order keys. No online/concurrent migration, durability, crash recovery, network, authentication, replication or distributed transaction protocol. Original scenarios, program and diagrams are teaching material.
